built_ideas.title: Foghorn
reasons: Unpainted monochrome prototype with no visible suit/number differentiation looks like an unfinished CAD test, not a real product.
Bluffing/reading trump signals is too cerebral for a 6-year-old and risks accusations of unfair play.
Looks like unpainted plastic prototype parts, not a finished colorful kids' game—no visual appeal at a glance.
Raw unpainted prototype parts with no colors, box, or finish—zero shelf charm or giftable polish.
Uniform terracotta-brown blank tiles show zero color variation or finish quality — nothing shelf-worthy or photogenic here.
Physical mock is just brown blanks with no dial, suits, or numbers—can't assess if trump-passing creates real strategic tension.
Photo shows only unpainted test tiles/dial, no card faces visible—can't sell a table on it sight unseen.
Only tiles/dial/box shown as bare parts—no visible scoring or solo variant to sustain repeat solo play.
Trick-taking-plus-dial twist is thin; photo shows unpainted generic tiles/frame, no differentiated production value.
No visible scoring depth or dial mechanism shown; components look like generic tile molds, no optimization system to master.
Bare uncolored prototype blocks feel cold and unfinished, not like the warm classic card/tile games I grew up with.
Just plain terracotta tiles with a spinner dial—no striking visuals or novel components a KS backer craves.
Same trick-taking bones I already own; a spun trump dial isn't enough to be genuinely novel.
Only plain wood-toned tiles and a dial, no minis or varied textures—reads as cheap, not value-packed.
Raw monochrome brown prototype pieces with no color, art, or graphics — zero shareable vibe for a 10-second clip.
Unpainted, undifferentiated tiles show no suits/numbers at a glance—unreadable for fast-teach, high-wear cafe play.
Unglazed terracotta-brick tiles look like raw hardware store samples, not shelf-worthy decor.
No visible cards/tiles or dial mechanism shown—can't assess balance, skill depth, or competitive integrity from unmarked blocks.
Winner-sets-next-trump is old ground (Fox in the Forest, Trumps); unpainted blank prototype shows no dial, faces, or thematic polish.
Unpainted monochrome prototype hides the suits/dial that make the bluffing hook legible—nothing here proves it's fun.
